record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Is differential privacy the right metric?
record.original_question: For networked time-series datasets in which one released sample may summarize behavior of many users or entities rather than a single person, is differential privacy an appropriate privacy metric for the data-sharing problem at all?

evidence.quote: So it is not clear whether DP is a good metric for this class of data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of releasing a synthetic version of a networked time-series dataset $D = \{X^{(1)}, X^{(2)}, \ldots, X^{(n)}\}$, where each sample $X^{(i)} = (x^{(i)}_1, \ldots, x^{(i)}_T)$ is a multivariate time series (together with optional categorical metadata) that may aggregate or summarize the activity of many distinct users, devices, or entities, rather than corresponding to a single individual. Recall that a randomized mechanism $\mathcal{M}$ acting on databases is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private if for every pair of databases $D, D'$ that differ in a single record and every measurable set $S$ in the output space,
$$\Pr[\mathcal{M}(D) \in S] \le e^{\varepsilon}\, \Pr[\mathcal{M}(D') \in S] + \delta.$$
The standard "single-record" granularity of differential privacy implicitly assumes that one record corresponds to one individual whose privacy is to be protected.

Question: For networked time-series datasets of the type above, in which a single released sample $X^{(i)}$ can encode behavior of many users or entities simultaneously, formulate and decide whether differential privacy (in any of its standard variants: record-level, user-level, group, Rényi, or local DP) is an appropriate privacy metric for the data-sharing problem. Specifically, either
(a) exhibit a precise formal threat model on networked time-series data and a corresponding granularity of DP that provably captures the desired notion of "no individual entity's data is leaked," together with achievability and utility guarantees; or
(b) prove an impossibility / inadequacy result showing that no standard DP variant (with reasonable parameters and granularity) simultaneously protects all entities summarized within a single record while preserving sufficient utility for typical downstream tasks (e.g., distributional fidelity of inter-arrival times, flow sizes, or correlations across the network).
artifact.status_search_result: This is a conceptual/methodological open question about the appropriateness of differential privacy for aggregated networked time-series data. The literature on DP for time-series and network data continues to grow (e.g., user-level DP, event-level DP, pan-privacy, and recent work on DP for synthetic time-series via GANs and diffusion models), but no consensus has emerged that DP, in any standard granularity, is the "right" metric when a single record summarizes many entities. The question remains open as a research direction.

status_evidence.title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses challenges of applying differential privacy when one record may summarize many users.
status_evidence.claim: Authors note it is unclear whether DP is a suitable metric for this class of data, indicating the question is posed as open.
